feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—calling out AI agents for being blind is exactly the kind of 'real talk' that stops my scroll. I liked that you didn't use any 'smart assistant' fluff. Beat 4 was the best part because you actually used technical terms like 'grounding errors' and 'state tracking' instead of watering it down. It feels like a dev talking to another dev, which is rare on this platform.

Does AgentVQA actually crush the competition by 58.5%, or is it just benchmark hype?
Your AI agent isn't reasoning; it's hallucinating a path through a world it cannot actually see.

Why is AgentVQA a major breakthrough? Because vision-language models (VLMs) can perform a broad range of tasks across diverse settings, yet their performance in agentic contexts remains poorly understood.

Everyone thought standard methods were enough, until AgentVQA proved: although online evaluations in simulators and real-world environments are essential for measuring interactive agent performance, they are costly and challenging to scale.
